classification.difficultyReason: Select and connect isosceles/equilateral angle facts, an unsignposted AAS proof for equal outside basepieces, a length equation and parallel/vertical angle chains across four supplied figures.

content.prompt: Find the values of $x$, $y$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above C on the left and B to the right. Matching double ticks on AC and CB.
spec.mathematics: AC=5 cm, AB=x, CB=y, angle ACB=60 degrees; angles A and B labelled alpha and beta.

answer.worked:
$AC=CB$, so $y=5\text{ cm}$ and $\alpha=\beta$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\beta=60^\circ$. All three angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral and $x=5\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above, C lower left and B lower right. Matching double ticks on AC and AB.
spec.mathematics: AC=x, AB=9 cm, angle ABC=70 degrees; angles C and A labelled alpha and beta.

answer.worked:
$AC=AB$, so $x=9\text{ cm}$ and $\alpha=70^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).

$$\begin{align*}\beta+70^\circ+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Outer triangle AEB subdivided by AD and AC, with E,D,C,B collinear. Two separate base dimension arrows and two equality-mark families are retained.
spec.mathematics: AE=AB=1142 mm; AD=AC; angle AEB=60 degrees; angle DAC=30 degrees; angle CAB=alpha; angle ACB=beta; DC=530 mm; CB=x.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived lengths or angles shown.

answer.short:
$\alpha=15^\circ$, $\beta=105^\circ$, $x=306\text{ mm}$.

Use the equilateral outer triangle and the isosceles inner triangle.
answer.worked:
$AE=AB$, so $\angle ABE=\angle AEB=60^\circ$. The angle sum gives $\angle EAB=60^\circ$, so $\triangle AEB$ is equilateral and $EB=1142\text{ mm}$.

Since $AD=AC$, the base angles of $\triangle ADC$ are equal:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACD&=\frac{180^\circ-30^\circ}{2}\\\angle ACD&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
$D,C,B$ lie on a straight line, so
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-75^\circ\\\beta&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle ACB$,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-105^\circ-60^\circ\\\alpha&=15^\circ\end{align*}$$
Also $\angle EAD=60^\circ-30^\circ-15^\circ=15^\circ$. Thus $\triangle AED\equiv\triangle ABC$ by AAS, giving $ED=CB=x$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+530&=1142\\2x&=612\\x&=306\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallel lines ABC and GFE cross the extended sides of equilateral triangle BFD. Beta occupies the angle between the upward rays, gamma the upper-right sector and alpha the lower-right sector.
spec.mathematics: BF=BD=FD; ABC parallel to GFE; angle GFB=100 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, equality marks, parallel arrows and unknown labels.

answer.worked:
$BF=BD=FD$, so $\triangle BFD$ is equilateral and $\angle FBD=60^\circ$.

Since $AB\parallel GF$, co-interior angles give
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABF&=180^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle ABF&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\gamma=80^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles). Also $\beta=60^\circ$ (vertically opposite to $\angle FBD$).

Angles on the straight line $ABC$ give
$$\begin{align*}80^\circ+60^\circ+\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
